newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Shi'ite Moslems take protest to capital.
newsitem.headline: Indian Shi'ite Moslems take protest to capital.

text.p: Indian police on Monday used water cannon to disperse Moslem demonstrators protesting against the arrest of a Shi'ite leader who has led a campaign to end a 20-year ban on a religious procession.
About 400 chanting protesters tried to break through a picket blocking a road leading to parliament before police trained water on them.

The demonstration followed the arrest on Sunday of Shi'ite leader Maulana Kalbe Jawwad in the central Indian city of Lucknow, which has a high proportion of Shi'ite moslems and where the annual procession has been prohibited since 1977.
The Shi'ite leader has led the drive against the ban on the annual procession which marks the death of Prophet Mohammad's grandson Hussain.
The ban was imposed in 1977 after about 15 people were killed in clashes between members of the Shi'ite and Sunni sects.
Thousands of police have been deployed across Lucknow, capital of the populous northern state of Uttar Pradesh, since last week to enforce an indefinite curfew.
Twenty-three people were arrested over the weekend in Lucknow, bringing the total number of people detained in sporadic violence since last Thursday to 604, the Press Trust of India said.

After they failed to reach parliament in New Delhi, several hundred demonstrators, beating their chests and chanting, marched to a local police station where local religious leaders gave speeches. There were no arrests.
